task_summary: Define the interface contract (types, props, exports, and contract tests) for the 'Shared UI Components' module (id: shared_components). This module provides six reusable React components — Sidebar, CodeBlock, VersionBadge, VideoEmbed, PageLayout, CalloutBox — each with strict TypeScript prop interfaces matching the canonical type registry, named + default exports, and vitest smoke tests. The contract must be precise enough for downstream page components and the app_routing module to depend on.

findings.topic: Named + Default Export Pattern in React/TypeScript
findings.finding: The project mandates every component export both a named export and a default export. The idiomatic pattern is: `export function ComponentName(props: Props): React.ReactElement { ... }` followed by `export default ComponentName;`. This ensures tree-shaking-friendly named imports while preserving default import compatibility. The named export MUST come first; re-exporting default from a named is cleaner than the reverse.
findings.source: Project operating procedures; React community conventions
findings.relevance: All six components must follow this pattern exactly. Contract tests should verify named exports exist on the module.

findings.topic: Props Interface Design — Canonical Registry Compliance
findings.finding: The canonical type registry defines exact struct names and fields for CalloutBoxProps, CodeBlockProps, VersionBadgeProps, VideoEmbedProps, SidebarProps, and PageLayoutProps. These MUST be used verbatim. The CalloutType enum has three variants: 'gotcha', 'warning', 'tip' — these are lowercase string literal union types in TypeScript (not a TS `enum` keyword construct). ReactNode should be re-exported as `type ReactNode = React.ReactNode` or simply used inline. RouteEntry and RouteManifest are owned by app_routing and must be imported, not redefined.
findings.source: Canonical Type Registry in parent context
findings.relevance: Direct compliance requirement. Any deviation in field names, optionality, or type names breaks the contract.

findings.topic: String Literal Union vs TypeScript enum for CalloutType
findings.finding: For a small closed set of variants (gotcha, warning, tip), a string literal union type (`type CalloutType = 'gotcha' | 'warning' | 'tip'`) is preferred over `enum CalloutType { ... }` in modern TypeScript. String unions are more ergonomic, produce no runtime artifact, and serialize naturally. However, the registry says 'enum' — the contract should define it as a string literal union type aliased as `CalloutType` since the variants are lowercase strings, not PascalCase identifiers. This matches standard React prop patterns.
findings.source: TypeScript handbook; React community patterns; registry specifies lowercase variants
findings.relevance: CalloutType is owned by this module. The choice of representation affects every downstream consumer.

findings.topic: Cross-Module Type Dependencies — RouteEntry and RouteManifest
findings.finding: SidebarProps and PageLayoutProps reference RouteManifest (owned by app_routing). The shared_components module must import these types from app_routing, NOT redefine them. This creates a compile-time dependency. For contract testing in isolation, the test file can construct mock RouteEntry[] data without importing the actual app_routing module — but the production types.ts must use the canonical import path. A common pitfall is redefining RouteEntry locally with slightly different fields.
findings.source: Canonical Type Registry ownership rules; modular architecture best practices
findings.relevance: Critical for avoiding type duplication. The contract must specify the import source for RouteManifest/RouteEntry.

findings.topic: React Component Smoke Test Patterns with vitest + @testing-library/react
findings.finding: Smoke tests for React components should: (1) render the component with minimal valid props, (2) assert it does not throw, (3) assert key DOM elements are present (e.g., a NavLink for Sidebar, a <pre>/<code> for CodeBlock, an <iframe> for VideoEmbed). Use `render()` from @testing-library/react with jsdom environment. For components using navigator.clipboard, mock it via `Object.assign(navigator, { clipboard: { writeText: vi.fn() } })` or use `vi.stubGlobal`. For NavLink, wrap in MemoryRouter.
findings.source: @testing-library/react docs; vitest docs; React Router testing patterns
findings.relevance: Every component needs at least one passing smoke test. Router-dependent components (Sidebar, PageLayout) need MemoryRouter wrapping.

findings.finding: prism-react-renderer v2 exports `Highlight` (named) and requires a theme import. The CodeBlock component wraps `<Highlight code={code} language={language} theme={theme}>` with a render-prop pattern. The copy-to-clipboard button calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(code)`. The `language` prop should default to 'bash' since CLI commands are the primary use case. In tests, prism-react-renderer renders fine in jsdom — no special mocking needed for the highlight itself, only for clipboard.
findings.relevance: CodeBlock is a core component. The contract must specify the language default and copy button behavior.

findings.topic: Responsive Layout Patterns — PageLayout at 768px Breakpoint
findings.finding: PageLayout should use Tailwind responsive utilities (md: prefix = 768px). Common pattern: sidebar is hidden on mobile (hidden md:block) with a hamburger toggle, or sidebar collapses to a top nav. The content area uses flex-1 with overflow-y-auto. The contract should specify that PageLayout renders a Sidebar and a main content area with `children`, and is responsive to 768px. Implementation details (hamburger vs. collapse) can be deferred, but the contract should assert both sidebar and content regions exist in the DOM.
findings.source: Tailwind CSS docs; responsive design best practices
findings.relevance: PageLayout is the shell component. Contract tests should verify structural DOM elements.

findings.topic: VideoEmbed — YouTube URL Handling and Security
findings.finding: YouTube embed URLs must use the embed format (https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID). The component should either accept an embed URL directly or transform watch URLs to embed URLs. The iframe should include `allow='accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture'` and `allowFullScreen`. For responsive aspect-ratio, use Tailwind's `aspect-video` class (16:9). The title prop serves as the iframe's accessible title attribute.
findings.source: YouTube IFrame API docs; web accessibility standards (WCAG)
findings.relevance: VideoEmbed contract should specify URL format expectations and accessibility attributes.

findings.finding: A Tailwind pill badge is typically: `inline-flex items-center px-2.5 py-0.5 rounded-full text-xs font-medium bg-{color}-100 text-{color}-800`. The VersionBadge should render the version string, optionally prefixed by label. The contract should specify that the version text appears in the rendered output.
findings.relevance: Simple component but contract test must verify rendered text content.

findings.finding: With six components plus their types, a single file would exceed 300 lines. Recommended structure: (1) types.ts — all exported interfaces/types (CalloutType, CalloutBoxProps, CodeBlockProps, etc.), (2) one .tsx file per component, (3) index.ts barrel export. Each component file stays well under 300 lines. The types file re-exports RouteEntry/RouteManifest from app_routing for convenience. Test files: one per component or one combined smoke-test file.
findings.source: Project file size constraint; modular component architecture
findings.relevance: Contract must specify the file/module structure to ensure consumers know import paths.

findings.finding: The project mandates `import React from 'react'` at the top of every .tsx file. This is required even with React 17+ JSX transform because the project rules are explicit. Contract tests (.test.tsx files) must also include this import.
findings.relevance: Compliance requirement for all .tsx files in this module.

findings.topic: Edge Case: Empty Routes Array in Sidebar/PageLayout
findings.finding: When routes is an empty array, Sidebar should render an empty nav without crashing. This is a common edge case in navigation components. Contract tests should include a smoke test with at least one route entry but the component should handle zero gracefully.
findings.relevance: Sidebar and PageLayout receive RouteManifest which is typed as an array — empty arrays are valid.

findings.finding: jsdom does not implement navigator.clipboard. For CodeBlock's copy button test, use `vi.stubGlobal('navigator', { ...navigator, clipboard: { writeText: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined) } })` or `Object.defineProperty`. The test should simulate a click on the copy button and assert `navigator.clipboard.writeText` was called with the code string. Use `await` since writeText returns a Promise.
findings.relevance: CodeBlock copy-to-clipboard is a key feature that must be testable without browser APIs.

recommended_approach:
Define the contract as follows:

**1. Type Definitions (`types.ts`)**
- Export `CalloutType` as a string literal union: `'gotcha' | 'warning' | 'tip'`
- Export all six Props interfaces (CalloutBoxProps, CodeBlockProps, VersionBadgeProps, VideoEmbedProps, SidebarProps, PageLayoutProps) exactly matching the canonical registry — same field names, same optionality, same types
- Import RouteEntry and RouteManifest from the app_routing module; re-export them for consumer convenience
- Export `ReactNode` as `type ReactNode = React.ReactNode`

**2. Component Files (one .tsx per component)**
- `CalloutBox.tsx`, `CodeBlock.tsx`, `VersionBadge.tsx`, `VideoEmbed.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`, `PageLayout.tsx`
- Each file: `import React from 'react'`, named export function, `export default` at bottom
- CodeBlock defaults `language` to `'bash'`
- VideoEmbed uses `aspect-video` for responsive 16:9
- Sidebar wraps NavLinks in a `<nav>` using react-router-dom
- PageLayout composes Sidebar + children in a flex layout with md: responsive breakpoint

**3. Barrel Export (`index.ts`)**
- Re-exports all types from types.ts
- Re-exports all components (named exports) from their respective files

**4. Contract Tests (`__tests__/shared_components.test.tsx`)**
- One smoke test per component verifying render without crash and key DOM assertions
- MemoryRouter wrapping for Sidebar and PageLayout
- Clipboard mock for CodeBlock copy button test
- All tests runnable in vitest jsdom environment with no external services

**5. Key Constraints**
- Never redefine RouteEntry/RouteManifest — always import from app_routing
- String keys for CalloutType must be exact lowercase: 'gotcha', 'warning', 'tip'
- All files under 300 lines
- Composition over inheritance throughout
alternatives_considered: Single-file component library: rejected because six components plus types would exceed 300-line limit and reduce maintainability
TypeScript `enum` for CalloutType: rejected in favor of string literal union — the registry variants are lowercase strings, and unions are idiomatic in React prop types with no runtime overhead
Redefining RouteEntry/RouteManifest locally: rejected because the canonical registry assigns ownership to app_routing; local redefinition risks drift and violates the contract
One test file per component: viable but a single contract test file is more cohesive for verifying the module's public API surface — can split later if file exceeds 300 lines
Using CSS modules or styled-components instead of Tailwind: rejected because the project uses Tailwind (pill badge, responsive utilities referenced in requirements)
risks: Circular dependency risk: if app_routing imports from shared_components AND shared_components imports types from app_routing. Mitigate by having shared_components import only type definitions (type-only imports via `import type`), which are erased at compile time.
prism-react-renderer version mismatch: v1 and v2 have incompatible APIs (v1 uses default export `Highlight`, v2 uses named export). Contract should specify v2.
navigator.clipboard mock fragility: different vitest/jsdom versions handle global mocking differently. Tests should use vi.stubGlobal or Object.defineProperty consistently.
RouteManifest import path may not be finalized when this module is implemented. Mitigate by defining the import path in the contract and using a temporary local type definition in tests only.
YouTube URL format ambiguity: component may receive watch URLs (youtube.com/watch?v=X) or embed URLs (youtube.com/embed/X). Contract should document expected format to avoid runtime issues.
compliance_notes: All files must be .ts or .tsx — no Python, no .js
Every type, interface, function, and constant MUST be a named export
React components: export BOTH named AND default (e.g., `export function Foo() {}` + `export default Foo`)
Every .tsx file must include `import React from 'react'` at the top
CalloutType variants must be exact lowercase strings: 'gotcha', 'warning', 'tip' — verified against canonical registry
Props interfaces must match canonical registry exactly: same names, same fields, same optionality markers
RouteEntry and RouteManifest are owned by app_routing — import via `import type`, never redefine
All public functions require type annotations
Prefer composition over inheritance — PageLayout composes Sidebar, not extends it
Prefer stdlib over third-party libraries — only prism-react-renderer (specified in requirements) and react-router-dom (for NavLink) are acceptable third-party dependencies
All files must stay under 300 lines
Tests must be runnable without external services (no network, no real clipboard)
Use `import.meta.env.VITE_X` directly if any env vars are needed — never `(import.meta as any).env`
String keys in maps/registries must be verified against source of truth, never inferred from names
